Torus is headquartered in Utah and is expanding manufacturing at our 545,000\-square\-foot facility in Salt Lake City called GigaOne. **We are** **the world’s first mesh energy infrastructure, uniting communities through resilient, sustainable, and intelligent power.** We design, engineer, manufacture, install, and support our systems end\-to\-end, standing behind them throughout their lifecycle. Torus systems help reduce costs, lower emissions, and protect facilities from outages, while strengthening the security and reliability of the broader utility grid. Torus is committed to American manufacturing, engineering excellence, and building energy systems that last.

  

Torus has raised over $267 million from investors like Magnetar, Mercado, ICONIQ and Origin Ventures. This investor confidence reflects the strength of our team, technology as well as the scale of the problem we are solving.

  

At Torus, you will be part of something larger than a single product or technology. Your work will help build energy infrastructure that supports and strengthens our electrical grid, critical systems, industry, and communities for decades to come. We value accountability, collaboration, and clear thinking. We are looking for people who want to solve hard problems and build things that matter.

The **Senior Program Manager, Physical Security** will own and evolve the physical security program protecting Torus System sites and critical infrastructure. title: Utility Design Engineer
description:
The Utility Designer II position is responsible for directing, coordinating, and exercising functional authority for planning, organization, control, integration, and completion of telephone, electric, and/or gas projects within the area of assigned responsibility.

**ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Completes utility design projects by self or in conjunction with support staff.
* Completes detailed utility designs for electric and/or gas customers
* Collects field data
* Assembles drawings using AutoCAD
* Analyzes engineering sketches, specifications, and related data and drawings to produce final product
* Completes tabs and populates information in proprietary customer software.
* Completes permitting process with local authorities.
* Coordinates with construction crew for installation of facilities per the design.
* Coordinates with customers on all aspects of project.
* Reviews design for compliance with engineering principles, company standards, client requirements, and related specifications.
* Evaluates and approves design changes, specifications, and drawing releases.
* Controls expenditures and hours within limitations of project budget.
* Other duties as assigned.

* Prior experience in utility industry, preferably design related. An understanding of construction methods and basic utility design is required.
* Bachelors or Associates degree in civil engineering or civil technology are useful, but not required.
* Must have working knowledge of AutoCAD.
* Ability to read and understand DOT road plan and profiles and cross\-sections is required.
* Ability to manage numerous tasks/projects simultaneously.
* Ability to direct and work with other employees.
* Must be self\-directed and work with minimal supervision.
* Effective technical writing and analytical skills with attention to detail.

title: Energy Management Engineer
description:
GM Performance Power Units \- Concord, NC
  
Energy Management Engineer \- Onsite
  
Job Summary
  
GM Performance Power Units is seeking a highly motivated Energy Management Engineer to support the development, testing, and trackside operations of our Formula 1 Power Unit. Based in Charlotte, North Carolina, this role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to a foundational area of our F1 program and join a world\-class Electronics \& Controls team. The Energy Management Engineer designs the control and measurement strategies that accurately track and estimate fuel and electrical energy usage across the power unit, ensuring full compliance with FIA regulations. These strategies are implemented on the TAG\-700 control unit using the MA toolchain, forming a critical piece of the technical foundation that will lead to race wins for our advanced hybrid power unit, targeted for debut with the Cadillac F1 Team.
  
Key Responsibilities
  
Energy Measurement \& Estimation Strategy
  
  

* Design control and measurement strategies that accurately measure and estimate fuel energy consumption and electrical energy usage and electrical energy storage across the power unit. These strategies provide the foundation for compliant and competitive energy management across a race weekend.
* Develop signal processing, sensor fusion, and estimation algorithms that translate raw fuel flow, battery, and electrical system measurements into accurate real\-time energy accounting. Account for sensor tolerances, thermal effects, and other sources of measurement uncertainty.
* Maintain a thorough working knowledge of FIA Technical Regulations governing fuel mass, fuel energy, and electrical energy limits, ensuring that all measurement and control strategies are fully compliant and can be defended under technical scrutiny.

**Hanwha Energy USA**, headquartered in Houston, Texas, is part of the Hanwha Group—a FORTUNE Global 300 company and one of South Korea's most respected business enterprises. title: Senior Engineer Generation Interconnection
description:
As a **Senior Engineer – Generator Interconnection**, you’ll play an important role in evaluating new and changing generation across the MISO footprint. You’ll perform and manage power system studies that help determine how generation can reliably interconnect to the transmission system while serving as a technical resource for MISO’s interconnection customers, Transmission Owners, and neighboring RTOs.



This role combines technical power system analysis, project ownership, problem\-solving, and customer interaction. Depending on your assignments, you may also serve as the project manager for system impact studies, helping coordinate studies from kickoff through completion and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned along the way.


**How You’ll Make an Impact**



In this role, you will:


* Manage and perform system impact studies for generator interconnection requests in MISO’s Generator Interconnection Queue, evaluating the reliability impacts of connecting new resources to the transmission system.
* Review and evaluate projects proposed by MISO’s Transmission Owners, providing technical recommendations based on power system analysis and established reliability requirements.
* Serve as a subject matter expert on assigned projects, communicating study results, technical requirements, and project details to interconnection customers, Transmission Owners, neighboring RTOs, and internal teams.


**What Makes This Role Exciting**



Generator interconnection is at the center of a rapidly changing electric grid. In this role, your studies won’t simply live in a report—they’ll help determine how new generation projects move forward, what transmission improvements may be needed, and how MISO continues to maintain a reliable system as the generation fleet evolves.
